page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning matrix multiplication. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 138364.71 and a PassMark CPU score of 122858.65. Single-core performance is average to strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2119.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2205.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching a top-tier read-only small block speed of 10222.53 GB/sec and a large block read speed of 392.84 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates top-tier capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 222.4 million operations per second.

Given its high compute density and lack of bundled local storage or GPUs, the c8i.32xlarge is highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that leverage its advanced vector and matrix instruction sets. It is well-suited for large-scale software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database operations, and CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token generation rates. However, for workloads requiring persistent local high-speed storage or dedicated graphics acceleration, external storage attachment or GPU-accelerated instances must be utilized.
